newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan gold rates seen stable.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan gold rates seen stable.

text.p: Pakistani gold is likely to trade in a narrow range if the rupee maintains its present official rate this week, dealers said on Monday.
Noureen Hamid, marketing manager of ARY Traders, one of the largest gold importers in Pakistan, said the rate would not change much unless the rupee was devalued.
"If the rupee was devalued against the dollar then gold rates would go up," Hamid said.

Forex dealers say there is no sign of an imminent devaluation, with plentiful dollar inflows from abroad following Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif's appeal to overseas Pakistanis to remit at least $1,000 each to increase foreign reserves.
The rupee opened 0.04 up at 41.16 to the dollar in the kerb market on Monday, dealers said.
One bullion dealer said gold demand had not risen much despite the current wedding season, while silver rates remained unchanged last week.
